text:
alex: Quick heads-up — canary run after the scheduler tweak shows a TTFT bump on routes with hot KV shards. Not huge but consistent during burst windows. token_wait spikes look correlated with eviction chatter.

maria: ugh. which metric exactly? aggregate or token-level?

alex: token-level. I pulled a few spans — TTFT p50 up ~28% for /api/chat on canary under 2k rps. decode time stable, kernel_time up for some samples. Looks like kernel selection sometimes picks a slower kernel when kvcache miss+eviction is happening.

sam: can you paste the probe trace and the query you used?

alex: trace snippet (sanitized):
```
span: request.start -> request.first_byte (8ms)
span: first_byte -> token.decode (12ms)
span: token.decode -> kernel.exec (95ms)
tags: route=/api/chat, model=redwood/fast-8q, kvcache_hit=false, kvcache_eviction=true
logs: "eviction triggered for shard=12, reclaimed=128 entries, pause=10ms"
```

alex: PromQL I used to roll up token_ttft: 
```
rate(token_ttft_ms_sum{env=~"canary|prod",route="/api/chat"}[5m]) / rate(token_ttft_ms_count{env=~"canary|prod",route="/api/chat"}[5m])
```

ingrid: interesting — decode stable but kernel spikes when kvcache_eviction=true. could be kernel picker taking an int8 path that ends up suffering from memory thrash.

maria: do we have per-token kv_wait or eviction_delay metric? I don't think we surfaced eviction as its own metric yet.

sam: we have kvcache_reclaim_duration_bucket but not attached to token spans. attaching would make attribution much cleaner.

perf-bot: ALERT: ttft_p50 increased 30% for route=/api/chat in canary (last 15m) :eyes:

ingrid: proposal: add lightweight token-level labels: kvcache_hit (y/n), kvcache_eviction (y/n), kvcache_reclaim_ms; emit separate kernel_ms span tag. That lets dashboards slice TTFT into prefix_wait + kvcache_reclaim + kernel_ms + decode_ms.

maria: +1. we should also add a sampled stack trace tag for kernel selection when kernel_ms > 80ms so we can see which kernel was chosen.

alex: agree. also recommend a new Grafana panel: stacked waterfall per-token where stacks: prefix_wait, kvcache_reclaim, kernel_ms, decode_ms. Start with 1% sampling to avoid cardinality blowup.

sam: sample PromQL for panel p50 per component:
```
label_replace(
  histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(token_component_ms_bucket{route="/api/chat"}[5m])) by (le, component)),
  "component", "$1", "component", "(.*)"
)
```

maria: actionable items:
- add kvcache_reclaim_ms tag on reclaim path (ingrid)
- emit kernel_ms span tag at kernel handoff (sam)
- add 1% token sampling in tracer and flag when kernel_ms>80 for stack capture (alex)
- dashboard panel (maria)

ingrid: I'll put up a small PR to emit reclaim_ms today and wire a metric. keeping it opt-in for canary first.

alex: I'll add the tracer sampling and the kernel_ms tag; want to keep sampling config in feature flag.

sam: I'll instrument kernel selector to attach kernel_name and kernel_variant when kernel_ms>80. low-cardinality (kernel_name+variant only).

maria: thanks — once kvcache_reclaim_ms is in, rerun the canary 1hr spike test and check waterfall. if TTFT still bad we can try a kernel selector tweak or backoff on evictions. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

perf-bot: NOTE: created ticket PERF-1723 for "token-level kvcache eviction instrumentation + waterfall panel"

alex: tagging @ingrid @sam @maria for visibility. will follow up with PR links in this thread.

ingrid: posted draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/451 (wip) — adds reclaim_ms metric and opt-in config.

maria: great; leaving this thread open until we have waterfall output.

alex: thanks all.
